2-0091-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony, Biztos Urak! Az ír elnökségtől mi, Patrióták, azt várjuk, hogy az európai polgárok valós érdekeit tartsa szem előtt: biztonságukat és jólétüket. A biztonságuk garantálása érdekében az illegális migrációt megállítani kell, nem pedig menedzselni. Európának vissza kell szereznie az ellenőrzést a külső határai felett. A visszaküldési irányelv hatékony alkalmazása kulcskérdés lesz.

Az európai jóléthez a versenyképességünk visszaszerzése elengedhetetlen. Ehhez alacsonyabb energiaárakra és kevesebb bürokráciára van szükség. A következő uniós költségvetésben ellenezzük a mezőgazdasági és a kohéziós források csökkentését. Elutasítjuk a további központosítást, a bürokratikus kiadások növelését és az ideológiai alapú feltételességi mechanizmust, mert mára bebizonyosodott, hogy a jogállamisági feltételeket ideológiai alapon alkalmazzák.

Jól mutatja a Bizottság által alkalmazott kettős mércét az a mélységes hallgatás, amelyet az új magyar kormány demokráciát leromboló alkotmánymódosításai kapcsán látunk. A köztársasági elnök és az Alkotmánybíróság tagjainak elmozdítása, a parlamenti képviselők választhatóságának korlátozása Európában példa nélküli lépések, amik minden létező demokratikus és jogállami alapelvvel szembemennek. Az előző patrióta, szuverenista kormány évekig tartó alaptalan vegzálása után úgy tűnik, ennek a Háznak és a Bizottságnak csak szelektíven fontos a demokrácia és a jogállam.

Nincs helye kettős mércének és ideológiának a bővítés kérdésében sem. Nem lehet figyelmen kívül hagyni, hogy Ukrajna háborúban áll, csatlakozása pedig súlyos következményekkel jár majd az európai mezőgazdaságra, a munkaerőpiacokra, a kohéziós politikára és a biztonságunkra nézve. Mi, Patrióták az ír elnökségtől több józan észt és kevesebb ideológiát várunk.
2-0091-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, Commissioners! We, Patriots, expect the Irish presidency to keep the real interests of European citizens in mind: their security and well-being. In order to guarantee their safety, illegal migration must be stopped, not managed. Europe must regain control of its external borders. Effective application of the return policy will be a key issue.

Regaining our competitiveness is essential for European prosperity. This requires lower energy prices and less bureaucracy. In the next EU budget, we oppose the reduction of agricultural and cohesion funds. We reject further centralization, increased bureaucratic spending and an ideologically based conditionality mechanism because it has now been proven that rule of law conditions are applied on ideological grounds.

The double standard applied by the Commission is clearly demonstrated by the profound silence we see in relation to the constitutional amendments of the new Hungarian government that destroy democracy. The removal of the President of the Republic and the members of the Constitutional Court, and the restriction of the electability of parliamentarians are unprecedented steps in Europe that go against all existing democratic and constitutional principles. After years of baseless condemnation of the previous patriotic, sovereignist government, it seems that democracy and the rule of law are only selectively important to this House and the Commission.

There is no place for double standards and ideology in the issue of enlargement either. It cannot be ignored that Ukraine is at war and its accession will have serious consequences for European agriculture, labor markets, cohesion policy and our security. We Patriots expect more common sense and less ideology from the Irish presidency.

2-0092-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Szanowny panie premierze! Przede wszystkim chcę bardzo serdecznie podziękować panu premierowi za przedstawienie wizji prezydencji irlandzkiej. Rzeczywiście bardzo dużo ważnych wyzwań i trzymamy kciuki, żeby te cele zostały zrealizowane. Bezpieczeństwo niewątpliwie jest kwestią dzisiaj dla Unii Europejskiej, dla nas wszystkich najistotniejszą.

Natomiast ja chciałam skoncentrować się w swojej wypowiedzi na kwestiach dotyczących – wydaje się – najtrudniejszego zadania, przed którym stoi prezydencja irlandzka i również my wszyscy, czyli budżet Unii Europejskiej na następne lata, ramy finansowe na kolejną perspektywę finansową. To jest ogromne wyzwanie, ale też wiele znaków zapytania. Przede wszystkim, myślę, że wszyscy stoimy na stanowisku, przynajmniej w mojej grupie politycznej, że absolutnie nie może być mowy o tym, ażeby nakładać nowe obciążenia podatkowe na przedsiębiorców i na Europejczyków.

Mówicie państwo o tym, że trzeba zwiększać budżet. My również nie chcemy, żeby wydatki były cięte w tych najistotniejszych, najważniejszych dla Unii Europejskiej projektach, ale nie może się to odbywać kosztem Europejczyków. Nie może się to odbywać kosztem konkurencyjności przemysłu europejskiego. I to kolejne zadanie, na które chciałam zwrócić uwagę.

Wszyscy czekamy z niecierpliwością na propozycję rewizji systemu ETS. Od tego będzie zależało – to jest kluczowe – czy gospodarka europejska wreszcie będzie mogła rozwinąć skrzydła i stać się konkurencyjna, a nie tak jak do tej pory po prostu być gnieciona rozwiązaniami, które niestety sama Unia Europejska przygotowała. Trzymam kciuki, panie premierze, za państwa prezydencję i mam nadzieję, że będzie ona, tak jak wszyscy oczekujemy, niezwykle ważna, istotna i konstruktywna dla nas wszystkich.
2-0092-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Dear Mr. Prime Minister! First of all, I would like to thank the Prime Minister very much for presenting his vision for the Irish Presidency. There are indeed many important challenges and we keep our fingers crossed that these goals will be achieved. Security is undoubtedly an issue for the European Union today, the most important issue for all of us.

However, I wanted to focus my statement on issues related to what seems to be the most difficult task facing the Irish Presidency and all of us, i.e. the European Union budget for the coming years and the financial framework for the next financial perspective. This is a huge challenge, but also many question marks. First of all, I think that we all take the position, at least in my political group, that there is absolutely no question of imposing new tax burdens on entrepreneurs and Europeans.

You say that the budget needs to be increased. We also do not want spending to be cut in these most important projects for the European Union, but this cannot be done at the expense of Europeans. This cannot be done at the expense of the competitiveness of European industry. And this is another task to which I would like to draw attention.

We are all looking forward to the proposal to revise the ETS system. This will determine - and this is crucial - whether the European economy will finally be able to spread its wings and become competitive, and not, as before, simply be crushed by the solutions that, unfortunately, the European Union itself has prepared. I keep my fingers crossed, Mr. Prime Minister, for your presidency and I hope that it will be, as we all expect, extremely important, important and constructive for all of us.

2-0093-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, cher Taoiseach – cher Micheál –, d’abord un grand merci de cette présentation et de vos priorités, qui sont résolument ambitieuses pour l’Europe. Alors, ce n’est un secret pour personne: on a l’habitude de travailler ensemble. Vous êtes un membre éminent de la famille Renew, et vous ne serez pas surpris, donc, de m’entendre dire que les priorités de votre présidence – compétitivité, valeurs, sécurité –, eh bien c’est aussi la feuille de route de notre groupe politique, Renew Europe.

Alors, cher Taoiseach, oui, vous avez raison: avançons sur notre compétitivité, achevons enfin notre marché unique, investissons davantage dans l’innovation, simplifions nos règles, donnons à nos entreprises les moyens de grandir en Europe plutôt que d’aller réussir ailleurs, avançons sur le prochain budget européen! Le cadre financier pluriannuel sera un test de vérité: si nous voulons une Europe puissante, nous devons lui donner les moyens de ses ambitions. Avançons enfin sur notre influence géopolitique: en poursuivant notre soutien à l’Ukraine, en préparant l’élargissement de notre Union et en défendant, sans jamais transiger, l’état de droit et les valeurs qui fondent notre projet européen!

Je voudrais dire un mot sur un dossier plus précis, parce que votre présidence sera l’occasion de démontrer que l’Europe sait protéger sans renoncer à ses principes. C’est exactement le sens du règlement sur la protection des enfants en ligne, dont vous faites une priorité absolue, et je voudrais vous en remercier. Cela fait quatre ans – quatre ans! – que nous attendons ce texte. Il n’y a plus de temps à perdre, et nous comptons sur votre présidence pour conclure au plus vite les négociations sur la réglementation à long terme. Vous pourrez compter sur le soutien absolu de mon groupe politique sur cette question, qui est fondamentale.

Ces réformes, cher Taoiseach, elles ne sont plus une option: elles sont une exigence pour les citoyens européens, parce que votre présidence, elle débute dans une époque troublée. Le monde est redevenu brutal, la force veut remplacer le droit, les puissances s’affrontent, les démocraties sont défiés, et, dans ce monde, l’Europe ne peut plus subir. Face à cette brutalité, notre réponse doit être l’affirmation de la puissance européenne, mais d’une puissance qui nous ressemble: une puissance démocratique, une puissance fondée sur nos valeurs, sur nos libertés et sur l’état de droit. Ces valeurs ne sont en aucun cas un frein à la puissance européenne – et je sais que nous partageons cela –, elles en sont au contraire la condition, parce que l’Europe, elle ne veut pas être brutale – ce n’est pas ça, notre modèle –, mais elle ne veut pas, évidemment, non plus disparaître – et pour cela, il faut assumer délibérément le rapport de force. On ne renie en rien ce que nous sommes.

Alors, cher Micheál, vous le savez, vous pouvez compter sur Renew pour la réussite de votre présidence, et puisque l’Irlande est aujourd’hui à l’honneur, permettez-moi de citer l’un de vos plus grands écrivains, Oscar Wilde: «Le progrès est la réalisation des utopies.» Alors, faisons en sorte que, pendant ces six mois, nos utopies européennes deviennent des progrès bien réels!
2-0093-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear Taoiseach – dear Micheál –, first of all, thank you very much for this presentation and for your priorities, which are resolutely ambitious for Europe. So, it’s no secret: we’re used to working together. You are an eminent member of the Renew family, and you will not be surprised, therefore, to hear me say that the priorities of your presidency – competitiveness, values, security – are also the roadmap of our political group, Renew Europe.

So, dear Taoiseach, yes, you are right: let's move forward on our competitiveness, let's finally complete our single market, let's invest more in innovation, let's simplify our rules, let's give our businesses the means to grow in Europe rather than going to succeed elsewhere, let's move forward on the next European budget! The multiannual financial framework will be a truth test: if we want a powerful Europe, we must give it the means to achieve its ambitions. Let us finally move forward with our geopolitical influence: by continuing our support for Ukraine, by preparing the enlargement of our Union and by defending, without ever compromising, the rule of law and the values ​​which underpin our European project!

I would like to say a word on a more specific issue, because your presidency will be an opportunity to demonstrate that Europe knows how to protect without renouncing its principles. This is exactly the meaning of the regulation on protecting children online, which you make an absolute priority, and I would like to thank you for it. It’s been four years – four years! – that we are waiting for this text. There is no more time to waste, and we are counting on your presidency to conclude the negotiations on long-term regulations as quickly as possible. You can count on the absolute support of my political group on this issue, which is fundamental.

These reforms, dear Taoiseach, are no longer an option: they are a demand for European citizens, because your presidency begins in troubled times. The world has become brutal again, force wants to replace law, powers clash, democracies are challenged, and, in this world, Europe can no longer endure. Faced with this brutality, our response must be the affirmation of European power, but of a power that resembles us: a democratic power, a power based on our values, on our freedoms and on the rule of law. These values ​​are in no way a brake on European power - and I know that we share this -, on the contrary, they are the condition, because Europe does not want to be brutal - that is not our model -, but it obviously does not want to disappear either - and for that, we must deliberately accept the balance of power. We in no way deny what we are.

So, dear Micheál, as you know, you can count on Renew for the success of your presidency, and since Ireland is in the spotlight today, allow me to quote one of your greatest writers, Oscar Wilde: “Progress is the realization of utopias.” So, let's ensure that, during these six months, our European utopias become very real progress!

2-0098-0000.sourceText:
, от името на групата ESN. – Г-жо Председател, Европейският съюз бавно, но сигурно губи позициите си в световната икономика. Възстановяването на конкурентоспособността вече не е въпрос на избор, а на оцеляване. Нужна е по-благоприятна среда за инвестиции, предприемачество и индустриално развитие. Предприятията се нуждаят от опростени правила и достъпна енергия, а не от нови регулации.

Шансът на Европа е в изобилието от таланти на нашия континент. Смелостта на предприемачите, които продължават напред, въпреки недомислиците на зелената сделка. И те заслужават подкрепа. Деиндустриализацията не просто отслабва икономическата сила на европейските държави, тя накърнява достойнството на професионалиста, останал без работа, ограничава възможностите за по-младите поколения, а оцеляването на цели региони е изложено на риск. Укрепването на отбранителните способности е необходимо, но трайната сигурност изисква и активна дипломация, защото устойчивите решения и мирът се постигат чрез диалог. Не бива да забравяме, че овладяването на миграционните потоци също е в основата на сигурността.

Затова приветствам ангажимента на ирландското председателство за намаляване на административната тежест за развитие на единния пазар и изграждане на по-сигурна и достъпна енергийна система. Самата Ирландия показва как благоприятната среда за инвестиции, предприемачество и иновации се превръща в устойчив икономически успех. Именно по този път Европа може да възстанови своята конкурентоспособност и мястото си в световната икономика.
2-0098-0000.englishText:
, on behalf of the ESN Group. - Madam President, the European Union is slowly but surely losing its position in the world economy. Restoring competitiveness is no longer a matter of choice, but of survival. A more favorable environment for investment, entrepreneurship and industrial development is needed. Businesses need simplified rules and affordable energy, not new regulations.

Europe's chance lies in the abundance of talent on our continent. The courage of entrepreneurs who press ahead despite the setbacks of the green deal. And they deserve support. Deindustrialization not only weakens the economic strength of European countries, it undermines the dignity of the unemployed professional, limits opportunities for younger generations, and the survival of entire regions is at risk. Strengthening defense capabilities is necessary, but lasting security also requires active diplomacy, because durable solutions and peace are achieved through dialogue. We should not forget that the control of migration flows is also the basis of security.

I therefore welcome the commitment of the Irish Presidency to reduce the administrative burden to develop the single market and build a more secure and affordable energy system. Ireland itself shows how a favorable environment for investment, entrepreneurship and innovation translates into sustainable economic success. It is in this way that Europe can restore its competitiveness and its place in the world economy.

2-0105-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Das Motto der irischen Ratspräsidentschaft, Strength with unity, Stärke durch Einheit, lädt mich als Oppositionellen gerade dazu ein, den Vorwurf zu machen, dass diese Einheit ein Festhalten an einer verfehlten Politik ist. Und gerade das sonst so sehr EU-freundliche Irland leidet jetzt unter dieser verfehlten Politik. Zwei Beispiele: erstens einmal etwa die Migrationspolitik, die auch in Irland durch das Opt-in beim Migrations- und Asylpakt immer mehr zu einem Problem wird, und auf der anderen Seite etwa der Green Deal und die Auswirkungen auf Irland, die auf Irland sehr, sehr unangenehme Auswirkungen haben und dort die Landwirtschaft sehr auch in Stress bringen.

Aber ungeachtet aller politischen Diskussionen möchte ich Irland ausrichten: Sie haben ein wundervolles Land, Sie haben wundervolle Menschen, Sie haben eine wundervolle Kultur, und Sie haben alles Recht dazu, stolz auf Ihr Land zu sein.
2-0105-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen! The motto of the Irish Council Presidency, Strength with unity, invites me, as an opposition member, to accuse me of saying that this unity is an adherence to a failed policy. And Ireland, which is otherwise very EU-friendly, is now suffering from this failed policy. Two examples: firstly, migration policy, which is also becoming more and more of a problem in Ireland due to the opt-in to the migration and asylum pact, and on the other hand, the Green Deal and the effects on Ireland, which have very, very unpleasant effects on Ireland and are also putting a lot of stress on agriculture there.

But regardless of any political discussions, I would like to say to Ireland: you have a wonderful country, you have wonderful people, you have a wonderful culture and you have every right to be proud of your country.

2-0106-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, buongiorno Irlanda.

La Presidenza irlandese sulla competitività afferma certamente valori condivisibili, però è un po' carente, secondo me: non cita mai le microimprese, eppure, sono 25 milioni le microimprese europee, e generano il 20 % del prodotto interno europeo e hanno problemi enormi.

L'accesso al credito, anzitutto. Dal 2011, i prestiti bancari alle imprese più piccole sono crollati del 37 %, schiacciati da algoritmi di rating e da una regolamentazione sbagliata per l'asimmetria regolatoria fra le stesse imprese.

Infine, la concorrenza sleale della Cina è sussidiata dallo Stato e rovina i nostri distretti.

Inoltre, sul 28º regime, di cui sono relatore ombra, la sinistra in Parlamento ha avanzato modifiche ideologiche di impronta ipersindacale – peraltro prive di base giuridica – e di maggior rigidità per gli investitori, che vanno in senso contrario allo spirito della proposta.

La Presidenza come intende salvaguardare questo aspetto? Buon lavoro.
2-0106-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, good morning Ireland.

The Irish Presidency on competitiveness certainly affirms values ​​that can be shared, but it is a bit lacking, in my opinion: it never mentions micro-enterprises, and yet, there are 25 million European micro-enterprises, and they generate 20 % of the European domestic product and have enormous problems.

Access to credit, first and foremost. Since 2011, bank loans to smaller businesses have collapsed by 37 %, crushed by rating algorithms and misguided regulation due to regulatory asymmetry between the businesses themselves.

Finally, China's unfair competition is subsidized by the state and ruins our districts.

Furthermore, on the 28th regime, for which I am shadow rapporteur, the left in Parliament has advanced ideological changes with a hyper-union imprint - which however have no legal basis - and with greater rigidity for investors, which go against the spirit of the proposal.

How does the Presidency intend to safeguard this aspect? Good work.

2-0113-0000.sourceText:
Liebe Frau Präsidentin, Micheál Martin, Maroš Šefčovič, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Drei Punkte hat der Kollege hier hervorgehoben: wirtschaftliche Prosperität, Werte und Sicherheit. Wirtschaftliche Prosperität hat die EU selbst zerstört durch die unsinnigen Embargos gegen Russland. Unsere Unternehmen haben jetzt die teuersten Energiepreise, sind nicht mehr konkurrenzfähig auf den Weltmärkten, verlassen die Europäische Union oder gehen pleite. Gleichzeitig zahlt die Europäische Union an die Ukraine – 300 Mrd. Euro waren das in dem ganzen Zeitraum seit Anfang des Krieges.

Und wie viel geht in die Forschung, zur Förderung der Wirtschaft und der Prosperität? Der Forschungs- und Innovationsfonds bekommt 90 Milliarden, lediglich 90 Milliarden im gleichen Zeitraum, und mickrige 10 Milliarden davon sind für Start-ups. Wir müssen die Embargos beenden und die Wirtschaft und Innovation stärken.

Werte? Über welche Werte reden Sie? Gleich wird hier abgestimmt über das Verbot der EU-Partei, der stärksten Partei in Deutschland, auf Antrag der Kommunisten, Sozialisten und der Grünen: Das sind die wahren Feinde der Demokratie; hier werden demokratische Werte, europäische Werte mit Füßen getreten.

Und Sicherheit? Sicherheit in der EU? Ich bin gespannt. Erklären Sie das den zwei kleinen Mädchen und der Ehefrau von dem schwedischen Polizisten Christian Zedig, der neulich umgebracht wurde. Sie haben in der EU die Sicherheit der EU-Bürger durch die Massenmigration zerstört. Und nur wir, nur wir durch die Remigration, wir liefern bereits aus der Opposition, und wir beschützen die Bürger Europas.
2-0113-0000.englishText:
Dear Madam President, Micheál Martin, Maroš Šefčovič, dear colleagues! The colleague highlighted three points here: economic prosperity, values ​​and security. The EU itself has destroyed economic prosperity through the senseless embargoes against Russia. Our companies now have the most expensive energy prices, are no longer competitive on world markets, are leaving the European Union or are going bankrupt. At the same time, the European Union is paying Ukraine 300 billion euros in the entire period since the beginning of the war.

And how much goes into research to promote the economy and prosperity? The research and innovation fund gets 90 billion, just 90 billion in the same period, and a measly 10 billion of that is for start-ups. We must end the embargoes and strengthen the economy and innovation.

Values? What values ​​are you talking about? A vote is about to take place here to ban the EU party, the strongest party in Germany, at the request of the communists, socialists and the Greens: These are the real enemies of democracy; Democratic values ​​and European values ​​are being trampled on here.

And security? Security in the EU? I am excited. Explain this to the two little girls and the wife of the Swedish policeman Christian Zedig, who was recently killed. They have destroyed the security of EU citizens in the EU through mass migration. And only we, only we through remigration, we are already delivering from the opposition, and we are protecting the citizens of Europe.

2-0116-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, começo naturalmente por saudar a Presidência irlandesa e estou certa de que a cooperação com este Parlamento será estreita e profícua.

Sabemos também que uma das prioridades é o orçamento de longo prazo da União e sabemos bem, também, de um compromisso de um trabalho intenso e ambicioso com todos os líderes da União Europeia para que seja possível ter um acordo até ao final de 2026.

Como a Senhora Presidente sabe, para o Parlamento Europeu, para nós, é absolutamente claro que é preciso que esse acordo exista até ao final do ano.

Mas não é possível trabalhar no QFP olhando só para o lado da despesa. É importante olharmos também para a ambição orçamental e é preciso olhar para a receita. Falo, obviamente, dos novos recursos próprios que tornem o orçamento europeu mais justo, mais robusto e menos dependente das contribuições nacionais.

Não se pode fazer mais com menos e este Parlamento apoia a abordagem da Comissão de um cabaz para obter um acordo sobre novos recursos próprios.

Precisamos de uma União Europeia mais segura, competitiva e coesa e de um orçamento à altura dessa ambição. Novas prioridades requerem maior investimento. Uma Europa mais forte exige um orçamento também mais forte.
2-0116-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I naturally begin by welcoming the Irish Presidency and I am sure that cooperation with this Parliament will be close and fruitful.

We also know that one of the priorities is the Union's long-term budget and we are also well aware of a commitment to intense and ambitious work with all European Union leaders so that it is possible to have an agreement by the end of 2026.

As Madam President knows, for the European Parliament, for us, it is absolutely clear that this agreement needs to exist by the end of the year.

But it is not possible to work on the MFF looking only at the expenditure side. It is important that we also look at the budgetary ambition and we need to look at revenue. I am obviously talking about new own resources that make the European budget fairer, more robust and less dependent on national contributions.

More cannot be done with less and this Parliament supports the Commission's basket approach to reaching agreement on new own resources.

We need a safer, more competitive and cohesive European Union and a budget that matches this ambition. New priorities require greater investment. A stronger Europe also requires a stronger budget.

2-0123-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Premier ministre, au moment où il vous revient de présider les négociations sur le budget pluriannuel, nous voulons vous adresser un message clair: on ne construit pas la compétitivité en sacrifiant la solidarité ou en léguant une planète invivable à nos enfants. Car, comme le dit le proverbe irlandais: «C’est en nous abritant les uns les autres que nous vivons.» Aussi, tant que le Conseil ne renoncera pas à liquider le Fonds européen ou à rogner les Fonds de cohésion pour financer le Fonds de compétitivité, il n’y aura pas de consentement du Parlement européen.

L’autre clash annoncé, c’est sur l’écologie. Je vois bien les tentations de tuer le principe consistant à «ne pas causer de préjudice important» à coups de dérogations, qui permettraient aux bénéficiaires de l’argent européen de s’asseoir sur les dégâts collatéraux qu’ils font subir à la nation. Mais j’ose espérer que, après l’épisode terrible de canicule que nous venons de vivre, votre présidence portera haut cette idée que, si l’union fait la force, l’unité se forge dans la justice sociale et dans la responsabilité environnementale.
2-0123-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Prime Minister, at a time when it is up to you to chair the negotiations on the multiannual budget, we want to send you a clear message: we do not build competitiveness by sacrificing solidarity or by bequeathing an unlivable planet to our children. Because, as the Irish proverb says: “It is by sheltering each other that we live.” Also, as long as the Council does not give up liquidating the European Fund or cutting back the Cohesion Funds to finance the Competitiveness Fund, there will be no consent from the European Parliament.

The other clash announced is over ecology. I can clearly see the temptations to kill the principle of “not causing significant harm” with derogations, which would allow the beneficiaries of European money to sit on the collateral damage they inflict on the nation. But I dare to hope that, after the terrible heatwave episode that we have just experienced, your presidency will uphold this idea that, if there is strength in unity, unity is forged in social justice and environmental responsibility.

2-0124-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, aujourd’hui, nos agriculteurs n’étouffent pas sous le manque de promesses, ils étouffent sous leur accumulation. L’Union européenne est devenue une usine à contraintes. Le programme de la présidence irlandaise affiche de beaux objectifs: compétitivité, sécurité alimentaire, simplification. Dans les faits, elle recycle des débats interminables qui encombrent et étouffent encore un peu plus ceux qui produisent.

Nos agriculteurs et nos producteurs n’ont pas besoin de longs discours, ils ont besoin de revenus dignes et d’une vision à long terme. Pourtant, ils subissent une triple peine: des importations qui ne respectent pas nos standards, des coûts et des règles qui changent sans cesse et une bureaucratie qui est devenue hors de contrôle. On les enferme dans toujours plus de pacte vert, de De la ferme à la table, ou de baisse de la PAC, et d’écologie punitive.

Comment prétendre prioriser l’agriculture en réduisant et en désacralisant l’enveloppe de la PAC? Prenons l’élevage: ce n’est pas un problème à corriger, c’est une richesse à défendre, c’est un pilier de notre souveraineté.

Vous nous parlez d’autonomie, de facilité et de nouvelle agriculture sans jamais rencontrer, sans écouter et sans comprendre ce que vivent les agriculteurs. Nous attendons donc, pleins d’espoir, que cette nouvelle présidence entende les agriculteurs et défende une PAC forte, autonome, au service de la production et de ses producteurs.
2-0124-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, today our farmers are not suffocating under the lack of promises, they are suffocating under their accumulation. The European Union has become a factory of constraints. The Irish presidency's program displays some fine objectives: competitiveness, food security, simplification. In fact, it recycles endless debates which further encumber and suffocate those who produce.

Our farmers and producers do not need long speeches, they need decent income and a long-term vision. Yet they suffer a triple penalty: imports that do not meet our standards, costs and rules that are constantly changing and a bureaucracy that has become out of control. We lock them into ever more green pact, from farm to table, or lowering of the CAP, and punitive ecology.

How can we claim to prioritize agriculture by reducing and desacralizing the CAP envelope? Let's take breeding: it is not a problem to correct, it is a wealth to defend, it is a pillar of our sovereignty.

You talk to us about autonomy, ease and new agriculture without ever meeting, without listening and without understanding what farmers experience. We therefore wait, full of hope, for this new presidency to listen to farmers and defend a strong, autonomous CAP, serving production and its producers.

2-0125-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Panie Premierze! Było dużo uprzejmości jak dotąd. A teraz parę szczegółów. Jeden z europejskich think tanków wyliczył właśnie, że w 2025 roku Unia Europejska straciła 90 miliardów euro, dlatego że jest ogromna ofensywa przemysłu chińskiego w Unii Europejskiej i upadają firmy. Mówimy dużo o Zielonym Ładzie, a ja chcę powiedzieć bardzo wyraźnie: najpierw energia powinna być tania dla przedsiębiorców, a później zielona.

Zwracam uwagę prezydencji irlandzkiej również na to, że historycznie Unia jest w tej chwili w największym długu. Jeszcze nigdy Unia Europejska nie była tak zadłużona, jak jest teraz. Mamy ogromny problem, czego świadkami są wszyscy obecni tu na tej sali, bo w Unii Europejskiej upadają firmy albo przenoszą swoją działalność do Indii, do Stanów Zjednoczonych. Ostatnio austriacka firma napisała wprost, gdy głosowaliśmy nad pomocą z funduszu globalizacji, że ucieka do Indii, bo nie wytrzymuje z cenami. Na takie rzeczy trzeba zwrócić uwagę. Życzę powodzenia.
2-0125-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Mr. Prime Minister! There's been a lot of kindness so far. And now a few details. One of the European think tanks has just calculated that in 2025 the European Union will lose EUR 90 billion because there is a huge offensive of the Chinese industry in the European Union and companies are going bankrupt. We talk a lot about the Green Deal, and I want to say it very clearly: first, energy should be cheap for entrepreneurs, and then green.

I also draw the attention of the Irish Presidency to the fact that, historically, the Union is currently in the greatest debt. The European Union has never been as indebted as it is now. We have a huge problem, as everyone present in this room is witnessing, because companies in the European Union are going bankrupt or moving their operations to India or to the United States. Recently, an Austrian company wrote directly, when we voted on aid from the globalization fund, that it was fleeing to India because it could not cope with the prices. You need to pay attention to such things. I wish you good luck.

2-0127-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'Europa ha due grandi priorità.

La prima: combattere tutte quelle follie green ed ecologiste che abbiamo visto nell'ultimo mandato, prima tra tutte l'ETS, quell'odiosa tassa ambientale che fa danni continuamente alle nostre imprese e ai nostri cittadini. Fermare il Green Deal: questo serve per una migliore competitività europea.

E l'altra, che non è seconda a questa prima priorità, è quella della sicurezza dei cittadini, la loro sicurezza che i cittadini europei pretendono di avere per le loro strade, nelle loro città, nelle loro nazioni.

E si combatte con due modalità. La prima è una lotta attiva al fondamentalismo islamico – rispetto al quale troppe persone qui in quest'Aula non stanno parlando, e lo stanno dimenticando – e l'altra è quella della lotta all'immigrazione clandestina: dobbiamo rimpatriare tutti gli immigrati illegali, perché, altrimenti, i problemi di sicurezza peggioreranno giorno dopo giorno, come hanno mostrato i recenti attacchi.
2-0127-0000.englishText:
Madam President, ladies and gentlemen, Europe has two great priorities.

The first: fight all those green and ecological follies that we have seen in the last mandate, first of all the ETS, that hateful environmental tax that continually damages our businesses and our citizens. Stop the Green Deal: this is necessary for better European competitiveness.

And the other, which is not second to this first priority, is that of the safety of citizens, their safety that European citizens claim to have on their streets, in their cities, in their nations.

And we fight in two ways. The first is an active fight against Islamic fundamentalism – about which too many people here in this House are not talking, and are forgetting – and the other is the fight against illegal immigration: we must repatriate all illegal immigrants, because, otherwise, the security problems will get worse day by day, as the recent attacks have shown.

2-0133-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, EU-kuplassa eletään aivan toisessa todellisuudessa kuin missä tavalliset eurooppalaiset elävät. Irlanti on uusi EU-puheenjohtaja, ja tämän puheenjohtajakauden toimintaohjelma on tästä todellisuusharhasta täydellinen esimerkki.

Kun eurooppalaiset pyytävät päättäjiltä yksinkertaisia asioita, kuten turvallisuutta, kohtuuhintaista energiaa ja asumista sekä suojattuja ulkorajoja, mitä he saavat? Arvojulistuksia, LGBTIQ-ohjelmia sekä antirasismistrategioita. Tässä toimintaohjelmassa käytetään sivukaupalla tilaa siihen, mitä ihmisten pitäisi ajatella ja mitä arvoja omaksua. Nämäkö asiat valvottavat eurooppalaisia öisin? No, eivät toden totta valvota. Lakatkaa siis jo tuputtamasta näitä ideologisia ohjelmianne ja alkakaa huolehtia siitä, josta teidät on valittu pitämään huolta: siitä, että kansalaisilla on turvallinen Eurooppa, jossa leivän päälle saa muutakin kuin pelkän ylähuulen.
2-0133-0000.englishText:
Dear President, in the EU bubble we live in a completely different reality than the one in which ordinary Europeans live. Ireland is the new EU presidency, and the action program for this presidency is a perfect example of this reality bias.

When Europeans ask policymakers for simple things like security, affordable energy and housing, and secure external borders, what do they get? Declarations of values, LGBTIQ programs and anti-racism strategies. In this action program, space is used in the side shop for what people should think and what values ​​to adopt. Are these things keeping Europeans up at night? Well, they don't really control it. So stop pushing these ideological programs of yours already and start taking care of what you were elected to take care of: that the citizens have a safe Europe, where you get more than just an upper lip.
